---
title: "Before the day"
aliases:
  - /tracks/one-day-tools/before.html
---
Before the day you read the case study and check that the browser lab loads on the machine that you will bring, which takes about an hour. The day is worked mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with the data already in place, so there is nothing that you have to install. Installing R, an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) and the downloadable workspace is optional and takes longer, but this is the format that uses them most. Part 2 has a stretch on the IDE and Part 4 one on the report, and with the workspace you work through both on your own machine rather than following them on the shared screen.

## 1. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study, with its questions, data and selections, then SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses with the software that each analyst used, and how the results of the five were put on one scale. Every part of the day works on this case.

## 2. The browser lab

[Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Open the lab once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the R engine has loaded and the first cell shows a "Run Code" button, and run the cell of Task 1. If it reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set. If it does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the day.

## 3. R and the workspace (recommended)

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

This step is optional, and recommended for this day. Install R and an IDE, download the [workspace of the EU-frames case](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace), and run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure. You do this once. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met, with prompts that you can give an AI assistant.

## 4. Your IDE (optional)

[Read the module on the IDEs](../../companion/ide.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

If you installed the workspace, read [What an IDE does](../../companion/ide.qmd#sec-what) and the section on the IDE that you chose, and try [the six steps](../../companion/ide.qmd#sec-try) at the end of the module in the workspace of this case.

## 5. R from the beginning (optional)

[Read Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The first two sections of the module on this site, [R and the IDE](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-what) and [The console, the script and the report](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-surfaces), say what R is and where it is typed. If you have never written R, go on to [Objects and vectors](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/intro-r.html#sec-objects) and [Data frames](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/intro-r.html#sec-dataframes) in the module of the same name on the housing-audit site, which teaches the first steps on a small file of its own. The R tutorial of Part 2 starts where these sections end.

**By the start of the day** you have the browser lab loading on the machine that you will use and, if you installed it, the workspace opening in your IDE with its check script reporting no failure.
